source.title: Batch Normalization Amplifies Memorization and Privacy Risks
source.authors: Ngoc Phu Doan; Chong-Yan Gu; Ihsen Alouani

record.file_problem: The supplied text is full, though several appendix results are presented only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own BN versus no-BN results on memorization and clean test performance, showing a trade-off relevant to generalization. It does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The study's label-corruption, OOD, influence, and membership-inference results concern memorization and privacy, not the listed versions. Figures 22–23 and the accompanying text report the relation between memorization and clean accuracy; only that generalization-related result is recorded here. Other memorization and attack outcomes are outside the versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares normalization conditions for outlier memorization and privacy leakage, rather than testing a listed version. Partial label corruption and clean-test accuracy do not establish V1's comparison of fully random versus natural labels. Batch-size and optimizer ablations report memorization accuracy, not held-out performance; influence experiments do not test V8's removal intervention.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that BN amplifies atypical-example memorization and privacy leakage. Section F additionally reports a modest clean-test generalization cost from removing BN. Their proposed BNReg mitigation reduces memorization and leakage while preserving accuracy on non-corrupted samples.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares BN and no-BN training to investigate outlier memorization and privacy, rather than reproducing a listed version's method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that memorization varies with corruption ratio, architecture, dataset, batch size, optimizer, and normalization technique; these results do not test a listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: Section F reports that removing BN reduces test accuracy modestly relative to its larger reduction in memorization. Membership-inference experiments also show higher privacy leakage with BN, including on clean CIFAR-10 and at matched clean accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can amplify outlier memorization and membership-inference vulnerability while providing a comparatively modest clean-test accuracy benefit.

fits_no_version.finding: The batch-size and optimizer ablations compare accuracy on deliberately corrupted training examples, and the influence analyses measure prediction divergence or gradient norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization's amplification of corrupted-example memorization persists across tested batch sizes and optimizers and appears in influence proxies.

record.problems: The clean test-accuracy comparison is shown in figures without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. The study's main experiments emphasize deliberately corrupted or OOD samples, rather than the natural-label generalization conditions in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for listed versions: the paper does not test them. Other BN memorization and MIA results concern outcomes outside the listed versions; their reported figure values are not needed to represent the clean-generalization trade-off.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fully random labels alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance held-out accuracy for random labels under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited and broader tuning.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a predictor of training–test gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The study cites several original sources but supplies no result or specific counterargument testing their listed claim versions. A modest BN accuracy benefit does not challenge V1's coexistence claim or establish V8's causal removal effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance held-out accuracy on random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set-size and overfitting conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Compared models trained with BN and without BN; Figure 22 reports test accuracy alongside memorization accuracy.

conditions.value: various datasets; individual values are figure-only

rows.measure: Test accuracy; text characterizes the generalization cost of removing BN as modest while memorization falls substantially.
rows.value: Removing BN sacrifices modest generalization while substantially reducing privacy risk; numerical test-accuracy values are figure-only.
rows.note: The text states the direction and qualitative size of the clean-generalization trade-off but provides no recoverable numerical values.
rows.check: The BN versus no-BN test-accuracy comparison measures no listed version, so 'partial' is inappropriate. Section F supports the qualitative generalization cost, but numerical values and dataset-specific conditions cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The row pools multiple datasets.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
